standard_prerequisites.name: Sub-quotients of derived complete modules are derived complete, so the cohomology groups of a complex of finite free modules over a derived complete ring are derived complete
A complex whose cohomology groups are all derived complete is derived complete
standard_prerequisites.use: Lifts the cohomological completeness to K itself.

core_obligations: The parenthetical statement (I-adically complete rings are derived complete) is explained by the complete-derived-complete lemma, cited at the start of the proof (proof lines 26132-26134). A pseudo-coherent K is represented by a bounded above complex K of finite free A-modules; each cohomology group H^n(K) is a subquotient of a finite free module, hence derived complete since A is, by part (1) of the Serre-subcategory lemma (proof lines 26135-26139). Part (2) of the same lemma says a complex all of whose cohomology groups are derived complete is itself derived complete, so K is derived complete (proof lines 26139-26140).
proof_roadmap: Represent K by a bounded above complex of finite free modules over the derived complete ring (proof lines 26135-26137).
Conclude via parts (1) and (2) of the Serre-subcategory lemma (proof lines 26137-26140).
